subject.title: feat(nodes): route alerts to the active computer

question: Should OpenClaw adopt gateway-owned active-computer presence across node APIs, model context, and connection-alert routing as a permanent core contract?
rationale: The recipient defect is mechanically repairable, but code correctness cannot decide whether all proposed protocol, prompt, API, and delivery-policy surfaces should become permanent product behavior.

options.title: Adopt after repair and proof
options.body: Approve the complete contract after source-node exclusion is fixed and live multi-Mac evidence demonstrates active-first and fallback delivery.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Keep activity in node APIs and CLI while deferring model prompt projection or automatic gateway alert routing.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Keep the linked issue open and hold this PR until a different active-computer design receives sponsorship.

recommendation.title: Adopt after repair and proof
recommendation.body: Approve the complete contract after source-node exclusion is fixed and live multi-Mac evidence demonstrates active-first and fallback delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available feature-history and domain evidence connects this person to the affected macOS presence and native-node paths.
